facts.text: Everton was named by railroad officials after a man named Evert or Everett, though the exact namesake remains unknown.
Dye's Park, just south of downtown, houses the historic Dade County Courthouse—also called the Penn Cabin—the county’s first courthouse.
The 1921 Sanborn Fire Insurance Map of Everton shows the town’s layout, including labeled businesses and the footprint of the old courthouse.
Everton is one of five U.S. communities that share its name, with others in Arkansas, Indiana, New York, and North Carolina.
The town’s first mention appears in both the FIPS‑55 and GNIS databases, marking its official recognition in federal records.
Everton’s history is captured in a single 1921 Sanborn map available online, offering a rare, detailed snapshot of the town’s early 20th‑century streets.
